newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKMA changes LAF reference to U.S. fed funds rate.
newsitem.headline: HKMA changes LAF reference to U.S. fed funds rate.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority said on Wednesday it will use the U.S. federal funds target rate rather than the U.S. discount rate as a reference for setting Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) rates.
The change was made in order to align the bid and offer rates under the LAF, Hong Kong's discount window, more closely with U.S. dollar market interest rates, the HKMA said.
It said the federal funds target rate tracks U.S. market rates more closely than the discount rate, which tends to lag behind movements in U.S. dollar rates.
The HKMA said there is no need to adjust current LAF rates because the U.S. Federal Reserve did not alter the fed funds target rate at its September 24 policy setting meeting.
The Fed left the federal funds target rate at 5.25 percent and the discount rate steady at five percent.
The HKMA also cited other reasons for the change.
It said the funds rate has become as transparent as the discount rate since the Federal Reserve began announcing adjustments to the target rate in February 1994.
The funds rate also is a more timely indicator of U.S. monetary policy compared with the U.S. discount rate, the HKMA said. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843-6371
